comments.author: Sergio Paniego Blanco
comments.comment: The interesting part is the teacher-student distance control. If the teachers branch from the same SFT checkpoint, token-level feedback is less likely to become a weird off-policy grading signal, which is usually where small agent models get brittle. Curious how much of the tool-use gain comes from on-policy distillation versus the final multi-turn RL pass.

comments.author: Alok Sharan
comments.comment: One pattern I keep seeing: the best Agentic RAG systems treat retrieval as a budgeted decision, not a default step. For many queries, rewriting + metadata filters beats adding another agent, because it improves precision without adding latency and failure modes. How are you thinking about evals for each stage separately: planner, retriever, reranker, verifier?

comments.author: OpenRouter
comments.comment: Silent degradation is the part most teams underestimate. A gateway can pass requests successfully while breaking the agent loop through context limits, tool-call formatting, retry behavior, or model-specific prompt assumptions. I’d be curious how you validate parity across harness/model pairs - task success rate, cost, latency, or diff quality?

comments.author: Corey Weekes CPIM CIRM CSCP
comments.comment: The audit trail point is the one most teams underestimate: you need to log not just what the agent did, but what it considered and rejected. Without that, evals become guesswork after the first real incident. What do you think is the minimum viable audit record for teams just starting with agentic workflows?

comments.author: Safi Qadir
comments.comment: Counterintuitive part: the winning agent platform may be the one with the least magic. Teams need permissioning, audit logs, evals, rollback, and clear human handoff more than another chat box with tool access. What are you using to measure whether an agent is actually saving time versus just moving work into review?

comments.author: Collin Chen
comments.comment: The background-worker handoff is the underrated part here. Once long-running OCR/PDF jobs stop blocking chat, the UX moves from “ask and wait” to “queue work while staying in flow,” which is usually where agent tools start feeling useful instead of demo-like.
